source_title: Apple brings touchscreen to MacBook Pro, price and features explained in 5 points - India Today
source_excerpt:
Apple is finally changing how you use a Mac with the launch of its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, packing an OLED display and up to 24 hours of battery life.
Apple is finally bringing a touchscreen to the MacBook Pro , changing how users interact with its flagship laptop. After a nearly 20-year wait, the new professional laptops feature touch controls, OLED displays, and the highly capable M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
Here is everything you need to know about the new touchscreen MacBook Pro in five simple points: advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Apple's first touch display For the first time, you can tap, scroll, and pinch to zoom directly on a Mac screen. This is a massive upgrade for creators, allowing them to draw on designs, play virtual instruments, and edit video timelines without relying entirely on a trackpad. Apple calls this new screen "PROLED XDR". It uses a tandem OLED panel that offers deeper contrast, up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness, and a smooth 120Hz refresh rate for highly accurate colours. Price in India and availability These new laptops are aimed squarely at professionals who need extra processing power and display capabilities. In India, the 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M5 Pro chip starts at Rs 3,49,900, while the 16-inch model starts at Rs 4,09,900. If you want the more powerful M5 Max chip, prices begin at Rs 5,49,900 for the 14-inch and Rs 5,89,900 for the fully loaded 16-inch model. Pre-orders opened on October 28, and the laptops will hit store shelves on November 9. Powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips
For the first time, you can tap, scroll, and pinch to zoom directly on a Mac screen. This is a massive upgrade for creators, allowing them to draw on designs, play virtual instruments, and edit video timelines without relying entirely on a trackpad.
Apple calls this new screen "PROLED XDR". It uses a tandem OLED panel that offers deeper contrast, up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness, and a smooth 120Hz refresh rate for highly accurate colours.
These new laptops are aimed squarely at professionals who need extra processing power and display capabilities. In India, the 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M5 Pro chip starts at Rs 3,49,900, while the 16-inch model starts at Rs 4,09,900.
If you want the more powerful M5 Max chip, prices begin at Rs 5,49,900 for the 14-inch and Rs 5,89,900 for the fully loaded 16-inch model. Pre-orders opened on October 28, and the laptops will hit store shelves on November 9.
Under the hood, these laptops skip the base M6 chip and are instead powered by the heavy-duty M5 Pro and M5 Max processors. These chips are built to easily handle demanding tasks like video production, 3D design, and running AI tools directly on the device.
Users can also configure the laptop with massive storage options up to 16TB. Despite the heavy performance, Apple promises an impressive battery life of up to 24 hours. Dynamic Island replaces the notch
Apple has removed the standard screen notch and replaced it with the Dynamic Island, a popular feature from the iPhone. Sitting at the top of the display, the Dynamic Island brings Spotlight search, real-time updates, and Siri AI within easy reach. With a quick tap on the screen, you can accept an AirDrop file, control your music, or answer a call. Lighter design and the glowing logo returns
Lighter design and the glowing logo returns
The new MacBook Pro is slightly thinner and lighter than older models. For long-time fans, Apple has finally brought back the iconic glowing logo on the back of the lid. The laptop is also packed with connectivity options, featuring three lightning-fast Thunderbolt 5 ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, and a headphone jack.
It supports the latest Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 standards, and includes an upgraded 12MP Center Stage webcam alongside a six-speaker system with 50 per cent deeper bass.
In short, the first touchscreen MacBook Pro is a major step forward for Apple's professional laptops.
